labs.title: Create a governed Power Platform development environment
labs.summary: Create a Sandbox environment with Dataverse, restrict it to a security group, and scope a data policy to that environment in a simulated Power Platform admin center.
labs.scenario: Contoso needs a safe Power Platform environment for makers building prototypes. In the **simulated Power Platform admin center**, create **Contoso Dev** as a **Sandbox** in **Europe**. Add a **Dataverse data store**, restrict access to **PP Contoso Dev Makers**, and use English language and US dollar currency. Do not create a Production, Developer, or Trial environment for this test scenario. After the environment reaches **Ready**, create **Contoso Dev collaboration policy**. Put **SharePoint**, **Office 365 Outlook**, and **Microsoft Dataverse** in **Business**; block **Facebook** as the social connector; leave remaining connectors in **Non-business**; and scope the policy only to **Contoso Dev** with **Add multiple environments**.
learningObjectives: Create a Sandbox environment with Dataverse and a security group restriction
Distinguish Sandbox, Production, Developer, and Trial environment types for a test scenario
Classify connectors into Business, Non-business, and Blocked groups
Scope a data policy to selected environments and explain connector data group separation
prerequisites: Know what environments and connectors are in Microsoft Power Platform

components.title: Managed Environments
components.text: Managed Environments add premium governance capabilities such as environment groups, sharing controls, usage insights, solution checker, and data policy features. They can be used with any environment type; this lab only reviews the concept.

steps.title: Open the new environment wizard
steps.instruction: In the navigation pane, select **Manage > Environments**, then select **+ New**.
steps.explanation: Admins create separate environments to isolate apps, flows, data, and lifecycle stages.

steps.title: Create Contoso Dev as a Sandbox with Dataverse
steps.instruction: Create **Contoso Dev** in **Europe**. Set **Type** to **Sandbox** and **Add a Dataverse data store** to **Yes**. Do not choose Production, Developer, or Trial for this test scenario.
steps.explanation: Sandbox is appropriate for development and testing before production. Dataverse adds a managed data platform for business apps.

rules.description: Contoso Dev is a Sandbox with Dataverse
rules.failureFeedback: Create Contoso Dev as a Sandbox in Europe with Dataverse.

steps.title: Restrict access and confirm Ready state
steps.instruction: Set **Security group** to **PP Contoso Dev Makers**, keep **Language** as **English**, set **Currency** to **US dollar**, and confirm the state changes from **Preparing** to **Ready**.
steps.explanation: The security group limits access to the development team. Language and currency become base Dataverse settings.

rules.description: Security and Dataverse settings are correct
rules.failureFeedback: Use the requested security group, language, currency, and Ready state.

steps.title: Start a data policy
steps.instruction: Go to **Security > Data policies**, select **+ New policy**, and name it **Contoso Dev collaboration policy**.
steps.explanation: Data policies reduce the chance that makers combine sensitive data with unapproved connector groups.

rules.failureFeedback: Open Data policies and select + New policy.

steps.title: Classify connectors
steps.instruction: On **Prebuilt connectors**, move **SharePoint**, **Office 365 Outlook**, and **Microsoft Dataverse** to **Business**. Move **Facebook** to **Blocked**. Keep the default group for new connectors as **Non-business**.
steps.explanation: Business connectors can share data with each other but not with Non-business connectors. Blocked connectors cannot be used where the policy applies.

rules.failureFeedback: Move SharePoint, Office 365 Outlook, and Microsoft Dataverse to Business.

steps.title: Scope the policy only to Contoso Dev
steps.instruction: On **Scope**, choose **Add multiple environments**, select only **Contoso Dev**, then choose **Review + create** and **Create policy**.
steps.explanation: Scoping avoids disrupting production or unrelated environments while enforcing guardrails for the development environment.

rules.failureFeedback: Create the policy scoped to Contoso Dev only.

labs.solution:
1. Select **Manage > Environments**, then **+ New**.
2. Set **Name** to `Contoso Dev`, **Region** to **Europe**, **Type** to **Sandbox**, and **Add a Dataverse data store** to **Yes**. Production is for live workloads; Developer is personal maker work; Trial is temporary evaluation.
3. Set **Language** to **English**, **Currency** to **US dollar**, and **Security group** to **PP Contoso Dev Makers**. Select **Save** and confirm the environment is **Ready**.
4. Select **Security > Data policies**, then **+ New policy**. Name it `Contoso Dev collaboration policy`.
5. On **Prebuilt connectors**, move **SharePoint**, **Office 365 Outlook**, and **Microsoft Dataverse** to **Business**. Move **Facebook** to **Blocked**. Keep the default group as **Non-business**.
6. On **Scope**, choose **Add multiple environments** and select only **Contoso Dev**.
7. Review and select **Create policy**. Connectors in **Business** and **Non-business** cannot be used together in the same app or flow where the policy applies. **Managed Environments** add more governance features, but this lab only reviews them.
